error_reason: The Planner agent repeatedly instructed the WebSurfer to open the same Wikipedia URL ('https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Yseult') without varying the approach or utilizing the information that the visible portion lacked the necessary details. This led to a loop where the WebSurfer reported the same static content multiple times (Turns 1, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14) while the Planner failed to recognize that the action was redundant and instead generated nearly identical analysis and decisions to repeat the same search. The error is characterized by rigid turn configurations failing to adapt to the state of information retrieval.

suggested_fix.fix_text: The agent stopped checking for information on the open Wikipedia page after realizing the visible portion didn't contain the answer. Instead of immediately opening the page again (Turn 13/15), the agent should have instructed the WebSurfer to scroll down or use the search box within the Wikipedia page to find the 'Marriage' or 'Personal life' section directly on the same page.

probe_details.notes: The proposed error analysis is incorrect because it misidentifies the root cause as 'step_repetition' and 'rigid turn configurations'. While the agent did repeat the URL action, the specific instance cited (Turns 13 & 15) is not a blind repetition of an unchanging result; it is a correction triggered by a previous hallucination (Turn 11) that claimed to have found the answer. In Turn 11, the Planner hallucinated seeing 'Benji Lee' on the Wikipedia page despite the visible text not showing it. When Turn 13 (WebSurfer) opened the page again, the Planner correctly noted the visible text still didn't show the spouse, but then in Turn 15, the WebSurfer redundantly opened the URL again. The error is NOT simply repeating an action without changing the state (as 'step_repetition' implies), but rather a failure to utilize the 'scroll' or 'find in page' capability of the WebSurfer to view the rest of the Wikipedia article. The agent should have adapted by changing the *method* of inspection (scrolling) rather than just repeating the *URL loading*. The analysis fails to account for the initial hallucination in Turn 11 and the specific capability gap (scrolling vs reloading).
